passages.text: Encoded PowerShell (T1059.001) is distinguished from approved administration by parent process, user context, and what happens next. Interactive office or browser parents, encoded command lines, and follow-on network or persistence activity are more suspicious than a signed management agent launching a short, decoded script.

Investigation playbook: (1) recover the process tree for the alerting PowerShell PID, (2) inspect command-line encoding and script block content, (3) pivot to network and file activity in a tight time window, (4) look for persistence (Run keys, scheduled tasks) on the same host.

Ingress tool transfer often follows suspicious execution. A new outbound connection to an uncommon IP shortly after encoded PowerShell, especially on 443 with a non-browser process, is stronger evidence than the execution event alone.

Common encoded-PowerShell indicators: -enc/-encodedcommand, FromBase64String, hidden window style, and bypassed execution policy. These are prior knowledge, not proof that a specific incident occurred.

After confirming execution, check CurrentVersion\Run, RunOnce, and startup folders for newly written values whose data references the dropped script or an unknown URL. Persistence is corroborating evidence, not a substitute for the execution chain.
